title: Vaginal Discharge
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with profuse, frothy, yellow-green malodorous vaginal discharge, vulvar irritation, dysuria, and dyspareunia. Exam reveals strawberry cervix (punctate hemorrhages) and vaginal erythema. Caused by Trichomonas vaginalis — flagellated protozoan. Diagnosis: wet mount shows motile trichomonads (flagellated organisms). Vaginal pH >4.5. Whiff test may be positive. NAAT (PCR) is gold standard — more sensitive than wet mount. Treatment: metronidazole 2g PO once or tinidazole 2g PO once. Treat sexual partners (even if asymptomatic). Avoid alcohol during treatment and for 24h after metronidazole (disulfiram-like reaction). Screen for other STIs.
